META:og:title: Middle East and Central Asia’s economy to shrink in 2026 amid war, IMF says
META:og:description: Iraq, Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar face double-digit declines in GDP amid the fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran.
=== BODY ===
The economy of the Middle East and Central Asia is set to shrink in 2026 amid the fallout of the US-Israel war on Iran, with countries such as Kuwait and Qatar facing double-digit contractions, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The region’s gross domestic product (GDP) is forecast to contract by 0.3 percent this year, a sharp downgrade from the 1.9 percent expansion projected in April, the IMF said in its latest economic outlook on Tuesday.
Ronaldo waves Saudi-flag scarf after match interrupted by missile alert
AI could self-replicate on home devices within ‘months’, Anthropic says
Man dies after fall from Six Flags rollercoaster in Georgia
More than 100 foreign trekkers stranded by floods in Nepal’s Gorkha region
The IMF cited the prolonged disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a conduit for one-fifth of global oil supplies in peacetime, for the downgraded outlook.
Kuwait, Iraq and Qatar are forecast to have the most severe economic contractions, with their GDPs expected to shrink by 16.7 percent, 16 percent and 15.6 percent, respectively.
Bahrain’s GDP is forecast to contract by 11.3 percent, while Iran’s economy is projected to shrink by 7.6 percent.
Saudi Arabia, which has partially offset the hit to its energy sector by boosting oil exports through the East-West pipeline, is projected to record negative growth of 3.3 percent.
Kyrgyzstan is expected to have the strongest growth in the region, with GDP forecast to expand 9 percent.
The Middle East and Central Asia is the only region that is expected to experience negative growth in 2026.
Emerging and developing Asia’s GDP is forecast to grow 5.1 percent, while the economies of Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean are projected to expand 4.5 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively.
